issue.title: Performance policy mode parsing is not exact
issue.promotion_reason: current contained failing evidence is repeatable or deterministically sufficient and satisfies the frozen plan

root_cause_group.claim: The performance-policy parser accepts case-variant mode values despite the exact lowercase contract.

theories.claim: The project performance-policy parser incorrectly accepts case-variant mode values such as `ENABLED`, allowing malformed policy input to activate the performance stage instead of being rejected.
theories.basis: The parser lowercases the supplied Mode value before validation, although the governed contract requires Mode to be exactly `disabled` or `enabled` and strict boundary validation to reject malformed input [qa-v1-block-c60e8152c304432fc78d7a0c, qa-v1-block-ce45392d2ebc036986b89d13, qa-v1-block-27d2771fd1e216ea720fc578].
theories.confirmation_condition: Parsing `## Performance Policy\n- **Mode:** ENABLED\n` returns PerformanceEnabled without an error finding.
theories.refutation_condition: An additional case-sensitive validation step rejects `ENABLED` before the policy can be consumed.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The frozen parser excerpt does not represent the effective implementation or another mandatory validation layer rejects case-variant modes.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Inspect or add a deterministic parser test for uppercase and mixed-case mode values without invoking runtime dependencies.

evidence.summary: The policy parser lowercases Mode before checking the accepted constants [qa-v1-block-c60e8152c304432fc78d7a0c].
The project-index contract specifies that Mode is exactly `disabled` or `enabled` and requires strict invalid-mode handling [qa-v1-block-ce45392d2ebc036986b89d13].
